claim: The production-stack router's ServiceDiscovery abstraction has exactly two implementations, K8sServiceDiscovery and StaticServiceDiscovery, and the latter is explicitly documented as the path 'for non-Kubernetes deployments or testing.'
stance_target: existing production routers already implement a pluggable, non-K8s worker-discovery backend
quoted_support: For non-Kubernetes deployments or testing, configure static backends: routerSpec: serviceDiscovery: "static", staticBackends: "http://model1:8000,http://model2:8000"

claim: In production-stack's router architecture, ServiceDiscovery and RoutingLogic are separate, independently pluggable components wired together by app.py's initialize_all(), so routing algorithms (roundrobin, session, kvaware, prefixaware, disaggregated_prefill) are decoupled from how workers are discovered.
stance_target: the router's routing-policy layer can in principle be reused unchanged when swapping the discovery layer for a non-K8s implementation
quoted_support: Router Pod app.py initialize_all() -> ServiceDiscovery (K8s or Static), RoutingLogic (roundrobin/session/kvaware/etc), EngineStatsScraper, RequestStatsMonitor

claim: kvaware routing logic in production-stack requires an LMCache controller integration (lmcacheControllerPort) and serving engines configured with lmcacheConfig.enableController: true, coupling that specific routing policy (though not the discovery layer) to an LMCache deployment.
stance_target: not every routing policy is fully substrate-agnostic even when discovery is decoupled
quoted_support: routingLogic: "kvaware", sessionKey: "x-session-id", lmcacheControllerPort: 9000 ... Requires LMCache controller integration and serving engines configured with lmcacheConfig.enableController: true.
